models.title: F realization from independent normalized chi-square variables
models.summary: The owner defines an F variable as the ratio of two chi-square quantities divided by their respective degrees of freedom.

relationship.original_equation: F = (chi-square numerator / numerator degrees of freedom) / (chi-square denominator / denominator degrees of freedom)
relationship.translation_notes: The chi-square quantities, degrees of freedom and resulting ratio are dimensionless; do not swap the ordered degrees of freedom.

assumptions: The numerator and denominator are independent chi-square random variables with their stated positive degrees of freedom when interpreting the result as an F-distributed realization.
The denominator realization is strictly positive; the numerator is nonnegative.
limitations: The calculator evaluates one ratio; it cannot verify distributional assumptions or independence from scalar inputs.
This is not the same input contract as the two-sample variance-ratio statistic; its chi-square normalizations and distributional assumptions are explicit.
No F density, tail probability or critical-value calculation is performed.
